source.title: Cited galaxy-cluster stops for the Cosmic road trip tour
source.acknowledgment: This research has made use of the NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database (NED), which is funded by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration and operated by the California Institute of Technology.
source.notes: raDeg, decDeg, position uncertainty, redshift, redshift uncertainty and the reference codes are the NED 'Preferred' values copied verbatim from the ObjectLookup JSON response on the retrieval date; NED redshifts are heliocentric. sexagesimalJ2000 is the same position as printed by NED's classic object search page on that date. scripts/prepare_tours.py converts the redshift to a Planck18 comoving distance on the catalog's equatorial Cartesian axes with no peculiar-velocity or frame correction, so the cluster center follows the same redshift-space convention as the DESI positions around it and appears stretched along the line of sight like they do. This is a pinned reference for camera framing and captions, not a claim of the best current cluster parameters.

membership.notes: Plausibility check that the framed region holds DESI galaxies: accepted DR1 rows within radiusDeg of the NED center on the sky and |Z - redshift| < redshiftWindow, counted from the checksum-verified leaf metadata by scripts/prepare_tours.py. It is not a cluster membership catalog, a virial radius or a completeness statement; the count depends on the survey's coverage of that sky region.

clusters.name: Coma cluster
clusters.framingNote: The tour frames the center from three times this radius so the cluster core and its redshift-space stretch fill the view; 3 Mpc is a round framing choice, not a measured cluster radius.
